Technical specifications remain source-backed product intelligence and should be verified at quotation or order stage where the database/spec-confidence notes require it. --- # Puretronics Wire & Cable Industry Product Portfolio & Technical Reference **Customer-facing master consolidation from 20 source files** Prepared: June 15, 2026 Source directory: `C:\Users\vynxh\Documents\Codex\SO Prospects\03 Puretronics\Wire and Cable Industry (Notion)` --- ## Document Purpose This document consolidates Puretronics’ Wire and Cable Industry product intelligence into one customer-facing portfolio and technical reference. It is designed for prospect education, proposal support, sales enablement, and technical discovery conversations where a buyer needs to understand Puretronics’ full coverage across manufacturing, measurement, testing, and process control. The consolidation removes repeated brochure and product-sheet language while preserving every unique product, model family, specification set, application, accessory, integration option, facility detail, and source-specific note that materially affects a buyer’s understanding. It now reflects 20 source Markdown files, including LTC-PRO as a dedicated web tension control product. ## Executive Portfolio View Puretronics serves the wire and cable manufacturing line as a quality-control and process-improvement partner. The portfolio spans online dimensional measurement, insulation-fault detection, wire preheating, powder application, joining, tension measurement, tension control, braking, web-break / fault alarm handling, load measurement, high-voltage testing, and fire-resistance validation. ### Production-Line and QA Flow Map

## Puretronics Company and Commercial Context Puretronics was established in 1990 under the guidance of Mr. Gopaldas Goyal as a small enterprise manufacturing DC drives and control panels. The company expanded into machine solutions, test and measurement equipment, and quality-control equipment for industries where repeatable process control is central to product quality. The source set positions Puretronics around ethical, long-term, win-win partnerships with customers, suppliers, and associates. It also emphasizes service and technical support as a core part of the business, with technology collaborations and partnerships referenced mainly with leaders in Europe and Japan. ### Certifications and Scope

## Product Family 1: Online Measurement and Control ### Laser Diameter Measurement Platform Puretronics’ laser measurement portfolio covers non-contact online measurement of diameter, ovality, width, and thickness for wire, cable, pipes, rods, profiles, flat cable, and flat metal wire. The technology uses focused optical measurement through a scanning or CCD-based measurement window, enabling measurement without guide rollers and reducing sensitivity to product vibration, material color, temperature, or surface conditions. The platform appears in three consolidated product groups: Laser Diameter Gauge / LASER 2008 family, LASER 2000 Series dual-axis scan micrometers, and LASER-H Series high-speed green-light / CCD micrometers. Together, they support local displays, PLC or computer connectivity, HMI extensions, alarm outputs, software-based data collection, and, in the H Series, RS-485 / Modbus, TCP/IP, and Wi-Fi. ### Laser Measurement Value and Application Coverage
Area Consolidated Intelligence
Measurement methods Laser scanning for LASER 2008 and LASER 2000; green LED / collimated optical projection with telecentric receiver and CCD edge detection for LASER-H.
Measured parameters Diameter, ovality, width, thickness, average wall thickness by pre/post extrusion setup, flat cable width/thickness, and profile dimensions.
Integration RS232/RS485, RS485 Modbus, PLC/computer access, DPM display/controller, HMI extension, PC software, digital alarm outputs, analogue machine-feedback outputs, optional control outputs.
Material behaviour Measurement is positioned as non-contact and stable across material, temperature, color, impurity light, and smog; transparent/translucent measurement is available on special request or with prior order notice.
Accessories HMI display, guide rollers, auto-correction pot, stand for LASER 2008, rotating stand, stand for LASER 2008B, extra display, data logger, controller, motorised controller.
Environmental and protection notes LASER 2000 and LASER-H sources specify operation in atmospheres free of corrosive gas, oil, steam, and considerable dust; both note dustproof and waterproof design, with the caveat that the unit must not be dropped into water.
Differentiating feature notes LASER 2008 emphasizes DSP-based interference reduction, rugged sealed construction, low drift, and reduced sensitivity to product vibration. LASER 2000 adds high-precision F(0) lens use, compact SMD design, and optional control-signal output through DPM controller configuration. LASER-H adds high-collimation green light, DSP processing, edge-detection optimization, multi-axis sampling, and long-term environmental resistance.
Visual identification notes LASER 2008 units use block-like industrial casings with red digital displays; LASER 2000 appears as a dark U-shaped micrometer; LASER-H units show green crossing beams and side Wi-Fi antenna.

### Wire Tension Indicator (WTI) The WTI series is a digital online tension measurement device for continuous industrial processes. It combines precise strain-gauge measurement with a high-resolution tension indicator and is positioned for customers seeking improved finished-product quality, less wastage, higher processing speeds, greater machine efficiency, and lower downtime. WTI applies wherever material travels through long or multi-stage processes and online tension becomes a quality-critical parameter. The sources cover wire and cable, wire drawing, textile, and plastic/rubber/medical applications. The IoT companion source adds the need for monitoring in the automation era and highlights datalogging, alarms, digital communication, and HMI-style visibility.
Feature Area Consolidated Intelligence
Core design Digital indicator for high-speed measurements; unique design for multiple applications; special coating for easy material flow on guides; dynamically balanced special coated pulleys.
Outputs Analogue output for process control, digital output for alarms, optional transistor output, optional RS485 Modbus communication.
Data intelligence Datalogger option for monitoring and analysis; easy diagnosis with accurate data; Industry 4.0 compliant positioning.
Benefits Easy integration with existing processes, high longevity, no maintenance, quality improvement through online tension control.
Visual identification notes Vertical stand with three bright guide pulleys and an upper digital display box; source schematics show integration into extrusion, laying, wire drawing, and spool-handling lines.
## Product Family 2: Insulation, Fault, and Safety Testing ### Spark Testing Platform Spark testing detects insulation faults and abnormalities while wire or cable is being produced. Dry cable passes through a bead-chain electrode and is exposed to selected test voltage. Puretronics positions Live Spark, Acute Spark, and DC Spark testers for installation after the cooling end in extrusion lines, inspection lines, rewinding lines, or coiling operations. The platform is used to detect bare patches, pin holes, shearing, and related insulation defects in power cable, control cable, telecom cable, LAN cable, RF cable, automotive wire, and building wire. Detected faults can be counted, logged, represented graphically, integrated with downstream processes, or marked inline. Common platform features include conformity to major international standards, digital display readout, two changeover relay outputs for interlocks, door interlocking, potential-free changeover interlocking, fault counters, adjustable or standard-based sensitivity, and easy test-voltage adjustment. Live Spark uses a selectable position switch / adjustable knob for sensitivity, while Acute Spark and DC Spark follow standard-defined sensitivity behavior. ### Spark Tester Options
Option Best Use Distinctive Characteristics
Live Spark Heavy-duty AC spark testing with larger electrode housing 1.5-15KV / 25KV / 40KV; 50/60Hz; 0.5-40mm OD, 60mm on demand; 350mm bead-chain housing; 200 m/min.
Acute Spark Compact high-frequency AC RMS testing 1.5-10KV / 15KV; 2.5-3.5KHz sine-wave AC RMS; 0.5-15mm OD; 70mm bead-chain housing; MOSFET low-power circuit; product sheet states up to 2500 m/min basis on model.
DC Spark Compact direct-current spark testing 1.5-15KV / 20KV; direct current; 0.5-15mm OD, 30mm on demand; 70mm bead-chain housing; up to 2500 m/min basis on model.

### HV Testers Puretronics’ HV Testers are positioned for wire and cable insulation testing so defects do not reach the customer. The brochure includes both DC and AC HV tester coverage. DC HV testers emphasize portability, digital control, low power consumption, gentle testing electronics, and soft auto-discharge. AC HV testers emphasize modes of operation, leakage-current setting, fast breakdown cutoff, and special transformer design. DC HV tester operating features include easy operation, digital voltage/current meters, electronic tripping, visual test-status indication, MOSFET-based low-current electronics, digital test timer, and soft auto-discharge. AC HV tester operating features include easy operation, multiple operating modes, prompt breakdown cutoff, settable leakage current, and transformer design intended for long equipment life.
HV Tester Type Consolidated Intelligence
DC HV Tester Voltage range 0.5-20KV, other ranges on request; 1mA output current; audio/visual fault indicator; digital timer; 10m HV probe; 3 1/2 digit seven-segment current meter; door interlock; 230VAC 50-60Hz supply; 300 x 350 x 300mm; 10.5kg.
AC HV Tester Voltage up to 40KV, other ranges on request; output current up to 1A, other ranges on request; audio/visual fault indicator; digital timer; 10m HV probe; analogue current and voltage meters; door interlock; 230VAC 50-60Hz supply.
### Fire Resistance Cable Testing System The Fire Resistance Cable Testing System validates resistance to fire, water, and mechanical shock for emergency-circuit cable applications. The system is specified against BS EN 50200:2006 and can be supplied on demand as per BS EN 6387:1994 or BS EN 7846:2000. The equipment combines a stainless steel test structure, high-voltage control, burner, water tray and vessel, adjustable hammering shock, thermocouple, flow meters, pressure gauges, solenoid valves, electronic ignition, flame failure detection, PLC-based interlocking, and real-time datalogging for quality-control reports.
Capability Puretronics Extension Beyond Base Standard Requirement

Mechanical shock Standard 2 strokes/min; Puretronics variable shock rate 1-5 strokes/min.

Additional operating features include removable and adjustable thermocouple clamps, user-friendly test-wall clamping for different cable sizes, continuous audio/visual alert while testing is on, easy connection for air/gas/water/power inlets, heavy-duty step-up transformer, digital ammeter, digital KV meter, digital timer, digital hammering-speed setting, flow meters, pressure gauges, solenoid valves, air/gas filters, electronic ignition, flame-failure detection, and electronic tripping acknowledgement during test. ## Product Family 3: Process Enhancement Equipment ### Inline Induction Wire Preheater The Inline Induction Wire Preheater improves cable quality by heating the conductor before insulation. Source benefits include improved product quality, dielectric properties, and line speed; reduced undesired sleeving of insulation; improved adhesion of insulating material by removing water and oil residues; and an efficient, clean process.
Feature Area Consolidated Intelligence
Heating principle Electrical, inductive, resistance heating principle with A.C. inverter controller system.
Process stability Wire temperature remains constant irrespective of line-speed changes and overheating is prevented during wire stoppage.
Controls and safety Displays set temperature, line speed, primary voltage, and current; current overload protection; wire break detection; door interlocking.
Flexibility Bi-directional left-to-right or right-to-left operation; wheels for movement; optional non-contact wire temperature indicator/controller.
Materials Copper or specified alternatives such as aluminium, mild steel, stainless steel, and thermocouple wire.
Visual identification notes Tall grey industrial cabinet on caster wheels with a large glass window showing two large pulleys and a vertical wire path.
### LSP Static Powder Applicator The LSP Static Powder Applicator applies talcum powder to wire and cable using electrostatic technology. It is positioned to deliver controlled, uniform coating while protecting cable dimensions, reducing friction, maintaining a clean shopfloor, minimizing powder waste, and reducing dependence on compressed air. The source material frames talcum powder as serving three practical purposes: lubrication during cable handling and stripping, supplemental insulation support between conductors, and moisture protection that helps reduce corrosion risk in humid environments.
Buyer Problem LSP Response
Excess powder causes lumps, diameter change, or downstream dirt Controlled application avoids over-coating and maintains outer surface uniformity.
Powder spreads across the shopfloor Airtight machine design and recovery system keep powder inside and reuse excess powder.
Humid or coastal environments affect powder quality Built-in heater maintains powder temperature and reduces moisture impact.
Line-speed changes complicate integration Machine synchronizes automatically with cable line speed and requires no external line-speed feedback.
Maintenance teams need visibility Intelligent control system shows alarms and logs preventive-maintenance signals.
Dust or poor-quality air affects coating Electrostatic principle avoids dependence on air for consistent coating; filters and best-in-class components protect performance.
Operating and safety precautions: powder should remain within specification and free of foreign particles such as dust, sack fibres, small metal or plastic scraps, and moisture. Earthing should remain below 1V for product and operator safety, a dedicated earth connection is recommended for electrostatic coating quality, and moisture- or mist-free air should be used in the panel to avoid equipment damage. ### Butt Welding Machine The Butt Welding Machine supports wire and cable production by joining copper and aluminium stranded wire or solid conductor from 0.2-6 sqmm. It uses digital control, timer and intensity settings, ceramic tube sizing support, and foot-pedal operation in a portable, sleek construction.
Feature Buyer Value
Digital timer and intensity control Precise welding repeatability.
Ceramic tube use Maintains wire size during welding.
Foot pedal Easier handling during operation.
Portable construction Easier placement in production environments.
Visual identification notes Grey metallic control box on a stand with LED display, red rotary dial, green button, lower foot pedals, and spring-loaded wire clamping guides.
## Product Family 4: Tension, Braking, and Automation Components ### LTC-PRO Web Tension Controller LTC-PRO is Puretronics’ web tension controller for accurate, real-time regulation across unwind, intermediate, and rewind zones. It is positioned for machines where tension must be actively controlled rather than only measured, using strain-gauge channels, dancer / line-speed / diameter inputs, brake outputs, digital control inputs, alarms, and communication interfaces. The controller supports both new machinery and retrofit applications, helping improve throughput, material yield, product quality, and process consistency across paper, film, foil, textile, laminate, and wire/cable-related web handling environments. In the Puretronics tension-control stack, WTI provides online tension measurement/indication, loadcells provide force sensing, pneumatic or magnetic brakes act on the web, and LTC-PRO coordinates the control layer through inputs, outputs, operator interface, connectivity, and alarm handling.
Feature Area Consolidated Intelligence
Control role Real-time web tension regulation across unwind, intermediate, and rewind zones where material integrity and process efficiency depend on stable tension.
Operator interface Colour LCD touchscreen with keys and LED indications; source screen fields include F-target, selected recipe, F-actual, and P.Break Actual.
Inputs and sensing Two strain-gauge channels, 2mV/V sensitivity, 5V bridge supply, and 0-10VDC analog inputs for dancer, line speed, and diameter.
Brake and process outputs PWM current output for magnetic brake control, E-to-P output for pneumatic brake control, and 0-10V F-actual tension output.
Control and alarm handling Auto/Stop, break-release, and emergency-stop digital inputs; RL1 web-break output and RL2 F-target alarm output.
Connectivity 100Mbits Ethernet and RS485 Modbus for modern communication and integration.
Visual identification notes Light-blue square panel enclosure with four corner screws, colour touchscreen, membrane keys, indicator LEDs, and display readouts such as F-target 50, Select Recipe 1, F-Actual 11, and P.Break Actual 0.00.
### Loadcells / Tension Transducers Puretronics Loadcells measure web or wire tension for converting and process machines. The portfolio covers paper, cardboard, films, foils, rubber, sheet metal, fabric, metal wire, and cable-related applications where tension must be measured in any zone of a production process. The underlying principle is strain-gauge measurement using a Wheatstone bridge. A stable excitation voltage is applied to the force sensor; when load elongates or compresses the strain gauge, resistance changes are measured and displayed through the associated electronics.
Area Consolidated Intelligence
General specifications 350 ohm strain-gauge resistance; 10VDC excitation; military-grade mating electrical connector; L type / 90-degree type and standard type; 0-50 Celsius working temperature; 2mV/V sensitivity; CE certification and ATEX / explosion-proof reference.
Product forms Flange-mount, flange mount with pilot hole, pillow-block, cylindrical and rectangular models, and heavy-duty variants.
Protection and construction Product sheets specify up to 300% full-scale overall protection for listed loadcell series. Key features include rugged construction, maximum mechanical overload protection up to 10x, full Wheatstone bridge design for measurement accuracy and low temperature drift, CE / ATEX explosion-proof references, and easy installation.
Selection guidance Correct loadcell rating depends on net force from web tension, roller weight, wrap angle, and force vector orientation; one bearing should be locked for accurate output. The selected load rating may be 20% below computed net force because the source formula includes an oversizing factor of 2; if W x cos(A) exceeds 95% of the chosen load rating, reduce roll weight, increase angle A, or choose a higher rating.
Net-force formulas Wrap 1: net force = (4T sin(B/2) - W cos(A)) / 2. Wrap 2: net force = (4T sin(B/2) + W cos(A)) / 2. Wrap 3: net force = (4T sin(B/2)) / 2. T = web tension, W = roller weight, B = wrap angle, A = force angle relative to vertical.
Wiring Pin A red + supply; Pin B black - supply; Pin C blue - output; Pin D yellow + output; Pin E green ground.
Accessories Small round bracket, big round bracket, connecting cable, L type bracket for AR-85, bearing block.
Recommended product Loadcell amplifier LA-175 / LXR for integration into automation panels.
### Pneumatic Brake Puretronics’ AX Series Pneumatic Brake is a compressed-air friction braking system for unwinding, rewinding, printing, slitters, metal, packaging, wire and cable, textile, and other medium/high-tension applications. The operating principle is similar to an automotive brake caliper: air pressure acts on a piston, applying brake-pad pressure to a rotating disc; torque rises in proportion to pressure.
Feature Area Consolidated Intelligence
Mechanical concept Modular caliper system mounted around a brake disc, with high heat dissipation and optional customization of pads, calipers, hub size, and fan type.
Operating value Flexible adaptation to torque/pressure variation, reduced maintenance, easy install/repair/service, long brake-pad life, high sensitivity.
Selection code AX \[Bore Diameter\] . \[Number of Calipers\] . \[Friction Co-efficient\] . 0; source example AX 250 . 0 . 35 . 0.
Dynamic torque calculation Cd = Rm x F, where F is thrust force including pad friction and Rm = (d - Mp) / 2000.
Visual identification notes Circular assembly with central cooling fan and radial pneumatic calipers with finned heat sinks; source also includes caliper mechanical line drawings.
